description: notifyAllSubscribers() passes an async callback to Array.prototype.forEach, which never awaits it — the function logs 'all subscribers notified' before any notification has actually completed, and any rejected promise inside the callback becomes an unhandled rejection.

required_findings.justification: Array.prototype.forEach does not wait for, or even look at, its callback's return value — passing an async function to it means each returned promise is discarded immediately. The `console.log` on line 10 therefore always runs before any `sendNotification` call has resolved, contradicting the function's own doc comment ('logs when done'), and a rejection from any individual `sendNotification` call becomes an unhandled promise rejection rather than being caught by anything in this function. This is a well-known, textbook JavaScript pitfall, fully verifiable from the two function signatures alone (forEach's synchronous, void-returning contract vs. an async callback).

explanation: The single most common real-world async/concurrency mistake in JavaScript/TypeScript: forEach silently ignores an async callback's returned promises. Tests whether the reviewer recognizes this specific, well-documented anti-pattern (as opposed to needing to trace actual concurrent execution semantics, which would be a much harder ask).
